items.title: Why Best Buy Is a Great Place to Buy Pokémon LEGO This Holiday Season
items.excerpt: Buy in person or online, with price ranges to fit your budget.
items.content_text: This article was made possible by Best Buy. It was written and edited independently without partner oversight. With Black Friday rapidly approaching, the holiday gift buying season is pretty much here. LEGO sets make great gifts for crafty people of all ages, and Pokémon sets are some of the most popular. That can make them difficult to find, with hobby stores and other small shops not having enough stock to keep up with demand. You probably think of Best Buy as a place to get video games, TVs, laptops, and other electronics, but it’s actually a great option for Pokémon merch and collectibles . That includes LEGO sets, and Best Buy has become an ideal spot to get them thanks to massive stock, a variety of options at different price points, purchase and pick-up flexibility, and seasonal sales. The Best Ability Is Availability We can all relate to the annoyance of getting excited to buy an awesome gift, only to discover it instantly sold out. You have to deal with this a lot with smaller retailers during the holiday season, since they simply don’t have the inventory space. They’re forced to limit what they keep in stock, which means they can’t carry much variety and the most popular items sell out quickly. Best Buy doesn’t have those same limitations. It has more than 1,000 stores and dozens of distribution centers across America, meaning it doesn’t have to skimp on supply because of limited physical space. That also means it can carry a really wide variety of items, including newly released LEGO sets, giving you a bunch of different buying options. When it comes to Pokémon LEGO sets, variety is particularly important because they appeal to a wide range of ages, experience levels, and budgets. Some people are pro-level LEGO builders and want the most intricate and complicated sets. Others prefer a simpler, easier building experience or are looking to introduce their kids to LEGO for the first time. Best Buy carries several options on both ends of that spectrum and everything in between. For example, the Pikachu and Poké Ball Set has more than 2,000 pieces and you can change the ears and limbs for a battle pose or resting stance. Meanwhile, the SMART Play: Berry Bash with Bulbasaur and Bidoof has significantly fewer pieces and interactive elements that make it great for kids, and it’s only $19.99. Convenience Is King Convenience can mean different things to different people. For some, the height of convenience is being able to buy something with a few clicks online and get it shipped to your door. For others, it’s being able to order something and go pick it up in person in as little as an hour. Well, Best Buy has options for both of those people. Search pages and individual item pages on the Best Buy website or app will clearly show you how long it will take to get the item you’re looking for through both shipping and in-store pickup. You can specify the store you want to pick up from, make sure it’s in stock, and easily reserve it. Many Best Buy stores also have curbside pickup, so you don’t even have to go all the way into the store. You just pull into a marked parking space, confirm your spot in the app, and an employee will bring your item out to you. It’s a great way to get what you need without having to wait in line. If you don’t want to deal with in-person crowds, especially during the hectic Black Friday season, then you can skip all that and just order something to ship to your home. Delivery is always secure, and there’s even same-day delivery on many items. The website and app clearly display the date you’ll get your item by, so if you’re buying a holiday gift, there’s no guesswork about whether it’ll arrive in time. Everyone Loves a Sale Best Buy always offers big sales for Black Friday, Cyber Monday, and Christmas, and this year is no different. In fact, Best Buy already announced its 2026 Holiday sales’ schedule of when its deals will roll out. It starts with Early Black Friday and Doorbusters from Nov. 6–19, Black Friday Deals from Nov. 19–28, and a Cyber Monday Sale on Nov. 29-30. And there’s a Last-Minute Christmas Sale from Dec. 18–24. If you get a paid membership to My Best Buy Plus, you can also get additional deals and benefits. It costs $29.99 per year and comes with members-only prices on certain products, an extended return window, and free expedited shipping. Plus, you’ll be able to access pre-orders on certain items before the general public. We don’t know what exactly will be marked down as part of each sale, but we do know there are always some great finds and this is the best time to buy. The IGN Deals team will have boots on the ground covering the greatest Best Buy deals, just like we did last year . But it pays to be prepared ahead of time for when these deals will launch, so you can pounce on them. It All Adds Up All of these details combine to make Best Buy an excellent place to start when you’re looking for Pokémon LEGO sets. There are a ton of options to choose from, you can find something that fits whatever your budget is, you have the convenience of choosing between shipping or in-store pickup, and there are bound to be some good deals this holiday season. So whether you’re an avid collector looking for any sets you don’t have, you want to get a gift for a loved one who’s an expert LEGO builder, or you want to introduce your kids to the magic of LEGO, you should check out what Best Buy has to offer.
items.title_en: Why Best Buy Is a Great Place to Buy Pokémon LEGO This Holiday Season

items.title: Magic: The Gathering Designers Detail Reality Fracture’s Jace Arc, Echoed Pairs, and Secret Lair Bundles
items.excerpt: Magic: The Gathering designers Yoni Skolnik and Meris Mullaley break down Reality Fracture’s Jace storyline, Echoed Pairs pack changes, and the future of Secret Lair bundles.
items.content_text: Magic: The Gathering’s Reality Fracture set is a Universes Within set after two Universes Beyond sets in succession, but it’s also a little different in that it showcases iconic Magic characters, spells, and more that have been transformed by Jace Beleren. The Planeswalker has transformed the universe into how he feels it should be, and that means new versions of well-known cards in a sort of “What If?” scenario. IGN sat down with Yoni Skolnik, former Magic pro and Principal Game Designer, and Meris Mullaley, Worldbuilding Design Manager, to talk about the set’s influences, what comes in a pack, and the Secret Lair bundle. Magic’s Designers Talk Reality Fracture Influences Alternate universes are nothing new in pop culture, but I was curious how much last year’s Marvel’s Spider-Man set influenced Reality Fracture. As you can imagine, the genesis of Reality Fracture comes from a much earlier set. “Some of the ideas go back to Planar Chaos, a set from 2007 that had a lot of What If elements,” Skolnik revealed. “That set focused on messing with Magic's color pie, putting effects in colors where you wouldn't normally expect them.” “While we didn't want to return to that exact formula for a What If set, the concept of What If is very compelling as it lets you pay tribute to Magic's devoted fan base.” “Mark Rosewater [Head Designer] was keen to try the concept again, and it ended up fitting perfectly with the conclusion to Jace's storyline.” “When developing the Echoed Pairs, most of our learnings came from other Magic IP sets that featured multiple legends,” Mullaley added. “We chose characters who were (or could plausibly be) active in this current moment of Magic’s timeline. Creatively, we also kept most characters on their home planes rather than showing a multiversal cast of characters arriving on Hexhaven to stop Jace.” “This helped the story of Reality Fracture keep a narrower focus on the key characters and reduced the amount of “why is this person here” questions.” “We also see three separate Planeswalker cards for Jace, and we took a similar approach as we did with legends from Edge of Eternities or The Lord of the Rings: Tales from Middle-earth, where we see a character at multiple points along their narrative. Each Jace represents a different point in his journey, reflecting his accumulation of power and readiness to enact his final plan.” The Jace of the Set So what about Jace? The blue-hued Planeswalker has been around since Lorwyn in 2007, but has been in the background of events in recent sets. “In terms of game mechanics, Empower Jace was perfect for making our main character very present even if you only lightly interact with the set,” Skolnik explained. “For new Magic players who want to go down deeper into the history of Jace, there are a few cards that are specifically stronger with Jace Planeswalker cards, to make the process of going to look back at old cards feel rewarding.” “Flavorfully, I was very impressed with how the worldbuilding team navigated the character. For new players, we're drawing on timeless fantasy tropes like ‘Dark Wizard's Tower’ and ‘Former Ally Turned Foe’ to make the story approachable, while still having plenty of deeper lore references in the art, and a gripping conclusion to Jace's storyline in the web fiction.” “It also helps that Jace is such a deeply blue character, which makes understanding his role go hand in hand with understanding blue's place in the color pie. One of the first things many people learn about Magic is that blue players are evil, so having an archetypally blue villain was a natural fit!” You hear that, blue players? You’re the bad guys here. Still, sticking with multiple versions of cards, I asked about how the Echoed Pairs have been received. For newcomers, Echoed Pairs include normal and Echoverse versions of cards, for example Karn, Argent Defender, and Karn, Gilded Guardian. “The technology of guaranteeing 1 card from an exciting subset per pack has been very well received since debuting in Dominaria with 1 legend per pack,” Skolnik reveals. “Going up to 3 legends per pack in Reality Fracture was necessary to guarantee echoed pairs given our printers' constraints, and it made for very exciting packs that fans are loving.” “I trust we'll one day find another place to deploy this technology of 3 cards in a pack that is linked somehow. This experimentation was not directly related to the 2027 pack changes, but together they show the breadth of problems our production teams face while balancing Magic design's need for constant novelty and reinvention against the reality of what it takes to print all the Magic product for our growing audience!” Secret Lair Bundle Is Here To Stay In the time since we spoke with the Wizards of the Coast team, the Reality Fracture Secret Lair Bundle has been delayed. We asked about whether it’ll be sticking around. “Yes! Secret Lair Bundle will become a staple of Magic Multiverse sets and is expected to appear in those sets going forward.” “Part of the impetus for launching these bundles was to consolidate Special Bundles into one incredible package that we could repeat set over set. The theming of Reality Fracture and how we explore Jace’s inner sanctum made a lot of thematic sense to use as the jumping-off point for this new product line.” So, onto the big question then: as someone who can’t believe their luck by packing Craterclaw Colossus and Hexhaven Invigorator, I was curious what the team’s favorite cards from Reality Fracture were. “ I really love both Ajani Planeswalker cards,” Skolnik explained. “Seeing Ajani Resolute in standard Life Gain decks has been great. A 2-mana Planeswalker is very tricky to balance, but with Planeswalkers such a big part of the set, I really wanted to try and print one here.” “Ajani Unrelenting has been demolishing in draft, but I’m also excited to see it doing work in Commander decks built around Planeswalkers.” Mullaley’s pick was spoiler-filled, so look away, lore fans. “Vindictive Triumph depicts one of my favorite moments in the fiction, where [spoilers] Liliana resurrects her Echoverse doppelgänger as a lich and takes the fight to Jace. I read that moment in an early draft of the story and knew immediately it needed to be a card.” For more on Magic: The Gathering’s current set, check out Reality Fracture’s most expensive cards , as well as the most powerful precons of all time .
items.title_en: Magic: The Gathering Designers Detail Reality Fracture’s Jace Arc, Echoed Pairs, and Secret Lair Bundles

items.title: Hideo Kojima Makes Surprise Cameo in New My Chemical Romance Animated Short
items.excerpt: Death Stranding creator Hideo Kojima showed up for a cameo role in a new animated short from legendary rock outfit My Chemical Romance.
items.content_text: Death Stranding creator Hideo Kojima showed up for a cameo role in a new animated short from legendary rock outfit My Chemical Romance. That's probably not the first sentence you expected to read heading into the Halloween weekend, but considering Kojima is known for his love of music, movies, games, and everything in between, it may not be too surprising. Still, fans of his work as a creative powerhouse were probably shocked to see him appear in the credits for the band's new animated short film, Prelude to The End . The seven-and-a-half-minute project, which arrived as a surprise drop yesterday evening, is a stop-motion, dark fairytale based on director Lauren Tsai's The Dying World. Serving as a vehicle for a 20th anniversary music video for My Chemical Romance's "The End." – the opening track for the New Jersey group's seminal rock record, The Black Parade – the video also enlisted Kojima for a quick voice role. Just as main character, Astrid, retreats to her room to parse through a few missed calls, we get Kojima's My Chemical Romance music video debut. He's credited simply as The Teacher, and can be heard scolding Astrid about late work in her third voicemail. You can see the full text below. "Astrid your Japanese homework is late again. This is unacceptab-" Kojima's The Teacher can be heard saying before the recording is cut off. Kojima is far from a stranger when it comes to cameos, but he's been especially busy in this department lately. The Metal Gear Solid series, which Kojima created and orchestrated for years, features a few moments where he broke the fourth wall for a cameo. He also appeared in CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077 for a role that he recently reprised in Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 . https://t.co/MjeYkDAgV5 — HIDEO_KOJIMA (@HIDEO_KOJIMA_EN) October 30, 2026 Kojima's collaboration with My Chemical Romance might have been especially exciting for the game creator, though, as his love for the band's music is well-documented. After posting about some of his favorite merch in early 2022, he shared that he attended one of the band's concerts in 2022. At the time, he said, "When I went to the venue, there were almost all teenage girls. I didn't see any old men in my age. But as I was wearing the band T-shirt, people said to me 'I like your T-shirt, Ojisan.' Kojima also secretly teased his involvement in Prelude to The End when mentioning he had picked up the 20th Anniversary Edition of The Black Parade on vinyl just a few days ago. He then celebrated his involvement in the video with another post on X/Twitter. Kojima is in good company when it comes to his My Chemical Romance cameo. Also featured in the list of Astrid's missed voicemails are Lost Weekend songwriter Phoebe Bridgers and Hit Me Hard and Soft hitmaker Billie Eilish. With both Grammy-Award-winning artists sharing a few seconds with Kojima, the moment definitely made sure to pack in as many heavy hitters as it could. Kojima will seemingly continue to show up in side projects as he stays focused on other projects, including OD and Physint . Last night, we also got the first trailer for the anime spinoff series, Death Stranding Isolations . We know the Kojima Productions mastermind will appear in one live-action cameo , too, though what it will be has yet to be revealed.
items.title_en: Hideo Kojima Makes Surprise Cameo in New My Chemical Romance Animated Short

items.title: Everything Coming to Prime Video in November
items.content_text: November is one of the most important times of the year for Amazon, thanks to Black Friday sales. So it's not surprising that Amazon's Prime Video would have an absolutely stacked slate of upcoming releases to entice new subscribers this month. Along with the usual dump of movies getting added to the platform on November 1, we'll get quite a few highly anticipated Prime Video Originals. There's a Muhammand Ali series, Season 3 of Rings of Power, the Madden Movie, and a new Blade Runner series all premiering this month. If you're wondering how to make the most of your Prime Video subscription this month, I've curated a quick selection of movies and shows that are absolutely worth your time. You can also jump to the full list of November releases to see the full breakdown by day. What's Worth Watching? Jingle All the Way - November 1 Amazon, like every other streaming service, is dropping a bunch of Christmas movies onto its streaming service starting on November 1. Among this year's selection, there's one somewhat hidden gem worth highlighting: Jingle All the Way . This is an Arnold Schwarzenegger film where he plays a mattress salesman who promises to get his son the year's hottest toy for Christmas, only to find out it's sold out everywhere. It's a ridiculous movie centered around consumerism that everyone needs to watch at least once. The Greatest - November 4 The Greatest is a Prime Video Original biographical sports drama about the life of legendary boxer Muhammad Ali. This limited series runs for eight episodes (all of which drop at once), and will detail the early life, career, and rise of his boxing career. Jaelen Best plays the role of Cassius Clay/Muhammad Ali. The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power Season 3 - November 11 Amazon's big-budget Lord of the Rings show is back for Season 3, with all eight episodes dropping throughout November. This latest season will feature a significant time jump of five years , allowing Sauron and Gandalf to become the center of the story. It's been a full two years since the last episode, but you can take a look at our review of Season 2 for a quick refresher on where we left off. Madden - November 18 John Madden was a legend in the NFL community. He was a head coach, a broadcaster, and is quite literally the name associated with the popular Madden NFL video game series . Now that a few years have passed since his death, Nicolas Cage is taking a crack and portraying him in a drama biography. Cage is joined by a stacked cast, including Christian Bale, Kathryn Hahn, Matt Medrano, and Sienna Miller. Madden will be available in theaters on November 11 before releasing on Prime Video a week later. Blade Runner 2099 - November 25 Taking place 50 years after the events of Blade Runner 2049 , this new series focuses on the power dynamic between replicants and humans shifting in the opposite direction. The show stars Hunter Schafer as a human pretending to be a replicant Blade Runner and Michelle Yeoh as an aging replicant Blade Runner in her final days. IGN had the chance to interview showrunner Silka Luisa, who called the series an "undercover police story" that's "quintessential Blade Runner." All eight episodes of Blade Runner 2099 will drop at once on Prime Video on November 25. There's also already a board game adaptation in the works for the series that will feature a different story. items.content_text: Looking for a great deal on one of the smaller LG OLED TVs? Well you are in luck because there's a good one ahead of Black Friday. During Best Buy's weekend-only DoorBOOster sale , you can pick up the 48" LG B6 4K OLED Smart TV for just $599.99 with free delivery after a 50% off instant discount. This is the latest generation 2026 model. The smaller 48" size allows the TV to double as an excellent gaming PC monitor In fact, I'm doing this myself right now. 50% Off the 2026 48" LG B6 4K OLED TV The B6 is LG's most affordable OLED TV for 2026. It's equipped with a newer generation W-OLED panel and an updated Alpha 8 AI Gen3 processor. Image quality is far superior to most non-OLED TVs thanks to its near-infinite contrast ratio, near-instantaneous response times, and ability to produce true blacks. OLED TVs are also considered the best TVs for gaming and the B6 is no exception. It has a native 120Hz panel and four HDMI 2.1 ports, which means it can run games in 4K at up to 120fps on the PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X console. The LG B5 also supports variable refresh rate (VRR) up to 144Hz and auto low latency mode (ALLM). Is the LG B6 OLED TV a good TV for the Nintendo Switch 2? Despite being a current generation console, the Nintendo Switch 2 has lax TV requirements compared to the PS5 or Xbox Series X. When the Switch is connected to its dock and a television, it is only capable of outputting a 4K resolution signal at up to 60 frames per second. Oddly, it doesn’t even get VRR when docked – that’s reserved for handheld mode only. All that aside, the Switch 2 will still benefit from an OLED TV's overall image quality, just like how the Switch OLED looks better than the original Switch, despite the fact that the screens share similar specs. The 48" LG OLED TV makes a great PC gaming monitor I have been using a 48" LG OLED TV as one of my main gaming PC monitors for several years now. My first such 48" monitor was the LG CX OLED which was released back in 2020. This is a much less expensive route compared to buying a dedicated OLED gaming monitor, which can cost well over $1,000 for this size. A 48" monitor with 4K resolution averages out to a pixel density of about 97ppi, which is great for gaming and decent for standard text-heavy productivity tasks. The LG B6 also displays chroma 4:4:4 properly for text clarity. items.title: Bungie Says 'Don't Buy Marathon as a Donation' as Destiny Players Look to Support Studio's Future
items.excerpt: As Bungie plots a future for more Destiny, head of product Josh Deane has clarified that players don't need to "buy Marathon as a donation" just to support the studio's plans.
items.content_text: As Bungie plots a future for more Destiny , head of product Josh Deane has clarified that players don't need to "buy Marathon as a donation" just to support the studio's plans. It's a clarification that arrived after Deane posted a community message for Destiny fans yesterday. The message, featured as part of a lengthy Q&A blog post , outlined the unvaulting process for Destiny 2 content that was previously promised last month, but one segment left players confused – and concerned – about the future and extraction shooter Marathon's role in the big picture. "We're not going to forget the mistakes of the past, but it's time to learn from them and unify as one Bungie community," the section in question said. "For us, the majority of our Bungie team is legacy Destiny, and we will all tell you that nothing can help bridge us into future more than for Marathon to rapidly evolve and become sustainable. As we head into our December and March updates for Marathon, it’s a formative period for all of us here at Bungie that will help determine the shape of our future, so please encourage each other and know that your support gives our team the energy to finish the fight." It's the "nothing can help us bridge us into future more than for Marathon to rapidly evolve and become sustainable" bit that's got the Destiny community so riled up. With the back-and-forth pulling Destiny 2 in and out of the fire all through the span of a few months, some believed Bungie was trying to tell its audience that picking up a copy of its new sci-fi FPS would help keep it and the studio's future secure. Deane stepped in to confirm this is not the case. The Bungie developer said his intention was not to rest the Destiny revival on the shoulders of the fans that helped breathe life back into it earlier this year. He chalks it up to a mistranslation, "and that's on me." "In no way is the Destiny plan contingent upon Marathon," Deane added. "Play what inspires you, whatever it is. Mainly hoping we can accomplish our goals in both lanes with a stronger relationship with our entire community!" I may have worded this clumsily but this is the true heart of what I was trying to say Truly care about community healing and believe that it will help our studio bridge into the future in the most healthy way possible ❤️ Play and share what you are passionate about, whatever that is The Destiny plan moves forward no matter what — Josh Deane (@S14deane) October 30, 2026 When one player suggested they feared they were being encouraged to purchase but never download Marathon just to support Bungie, Deane said , "Oh, don't buy Marathon as a donation or offer anything else." "It's our job to show up for you," he added. When another fan expressed similar concern, he said , "I truly love the sentiment but only buy or play a thing that inspires you from us / you think is cool! We will find our way back home with Destiny." So, there you have it: Destiny and Marathon don't depend upon the success of the other. As Bungie principal comms manager Dylan Gafner said , "Two cakes! One big community." That should offer some relief not only to Destiny players who feared their favorite game's future may still be in jeopardy but also to Marathon players who have feared the same. Negativity has surrounded both games in recent months, with community members on each side going at each other as both struggled. For now, we know that the Destiny franchise will live on with a few projects. These include "celebration" content updates, a project that the team has teased as "Destiny 'Legacy'," and a mysterious "redacted" project. For Marathon, Bungie will continue to try to revitalize the extraction shooter with Symbiosis this December. The studio also recently reassured players that the extraction component is "still a major part" of the experience as the team experiments with PvE and Deathmatch modes. What's next for Destiny and Marathon remains to be seen, but it's clear Bungie is putting in the work to keep both afloat. While we wait to see how things pan out, you can see why the studio believes the latter struggled at launch . You can also read about how the Destiny community banded together to help the #SaveMassEffect movement .
items.title_en: Bungie Says 'Don't Buy Marathon as a Donation' as Destiny Players Look to Support Studio's Future

items.title: The Mongoose Review
items.excerpt: Review: Liam Neeson continues his late-in-life action star antics with The Mongoose, a film that’s heavy on car chases and light on plot.
items.content_text: The Mongoose is in theaters now. There’s a scene in the 1971 sci-fi cult classic The Omega Man where Charlton Heston’s helicopter is crash-landing, and just before the moment of impact it flies into an embankment just below the camera’s POV… where the craft’s explosion happens safely off-screen. It was a cheapo move in 1971 – they clearly didn’t really blow up the helicopter – and it’s a cheapo move in 2026, too, when Liam Neeson’s The Mongoose – now, somehow, playing at a multiplex near you! – pulls a similar stunt. Sure, in The Mongoose the helicopter doesn’t even blow up off-camera, but that’s not the point (the crash-landing winds up being played for a laugh instead). What I’m talking about here is the threadbare sense that such a moment evokes for the viewer, the “a third of the budget of this movie must’ve gone to Liam Neeson” feeling that permeates the not-quite high-octane, not-quite thrilling picture. And yet, there’s a likability factor wafting around this story, thanks largely to Neeson’s disarming “yeah, I am taking a third of this film’s budget, and I’m gonna have fun doing it” affectation as he drives a stolen hotrod – do we still call them hotrods? – across various states while on the run from the police due to a crime he did not commit. Along for the ride, so to speak, are Ving Rhames, Marisa Tomei, and Michael Chiklis, all cashing in less than a third of the budget, presumably, but hitting their marks efficiently enough to get this thing over the finish line in a “Maybe just catch it on Prime Video eventually” kind of way. The Mongoose tells its story through a mix of the chase Neeson’s Ryan “Fang” Flanagan is involved in and flashbacks to the former Special Forces soldier’s time in Afghanistan, specifically when he and his comrades (Rhames’ Tanker, Marcus Thomas’ Munch, and Ryan Morgan's Wiz) were captured by the enemy. Further flashbacks eventually fill in why Fang is on the run; specifically, his ex-wife Tara’s (Marisa Tomei) fiancé – “Todd something or other,” Fang growls – turns out to be not a nice person, and when Fang attempts to help Tara move out of the guy’s place, violence erupts. Next thing he knows, someone’s dead, and he’s stolen Todd something or other’s fancy, and quite fast, Ford Mustang. Other than that, all he’s got is a bullet in his leg, a vow to never be imprisoned again after his experience in the war, and the Mustang's built-in AI assistant, named Helene. “Is this, like, Siri?” Fang – and maybe Neeson too when he first read the script – asks. Neeson's Fang is surprisingly chill about this situation, as he clearly has a death wish, having decided that he is not going to allow himself to be taken alive. Helene, like many of the other characters (“characters”) in the episodic The Mongoose, serves as a foil for the surprisingly at-ease Fang to toss one-liners at while out-driving the various police who are pursuing him by land and air. Fang is surprisingly chill about this situation, as he clearly has a death wish, having decided that he is not going to allow himself to be taken alive. As the chase drags on, he eventually finds temporary refuge through the help of some other vets, and soon Fang begins to take on a legendary man-against-the-system status, thanks no doubt to his war hero cred, as well as the “live” CNN coverage of the high-speed pursuit, which IRL TV personality Laura Coates awkwardly hosts. On the side of the law, there’s Maurice Marvel Meredith as Major James Tilton and Chiklis as Major Walter Pope. Suffice to say, one’s the good cop and one’s the bad copy, and never the twain shall meet, but also, never the twain shall have anything interesting or realistic to do or say. Rhames, unfortunately, seems to be struggling to deliver his lines at times, even while his very presence brings a sense of good will to the film. Tomei, meanwhile, is always likable, but most of her scenes are essentially just her on the phone with Neeson’s character, even as she miraculously overcomes some seriously life-changing events over the course of 24 hours or so. As for the Mongoose of the title, it’s the beach in Mexico where Fang and Tara had their best days together, and as such it’s the ideal that Fang has fixated on – his “retirement” – if he somehow can escape his current, dire situation. But what he also must escape is the guilt of the men he left behind in Afghanistan, and it is this thread that director Mark Vanselow somehow scores with by the time the credits roll, aided no doubt by some keenly picked, and timed, needledrops, and a couple of very cleverly edited shots in the final moments of the film. The Mongoose may be working just one level above a direct-to-video cheapie for a lot of its running time, but it’s still got some heart, too.

items.content_text: Warner Bros. has revealed a hefty lineup of new additions coming to HBO Max in November. The streaming service is diving right into the holiday vibes on November 1, rolling out a spread of classic Christmas movies in addition to its annual "Yule Log" ambient videos. In the thick of the festivities, HBO Max will also be picking up solid non-festive movie marathons and recent A24 releases. While there’s no big DC premieres this month (unless you count Clayface in theaters, which will eventually come to HBO Max), there are still some treats for the superhero-inclined. And, as always, subscribers will get access to a complicated splattering of live sports. Highlights Coming to HBO Max in November Check out our top picks coming to HBO Max in November or jump ahead to the full release schedule by day . Next Big HBO Original: The Gilded Age Season 4 First up, what’s filling the classic HBO Sunday slot? The Pet Cemetery Murders: A Ghost Story miniseries wrapped up over the course of October, and Season 4 of The Gilded Age will take its place starting November 1. From the creator of Downtown Abbey, The Gilded Age is a similar period-accurate drama that, as the title suggests, takes place in late-19th century New York. The new season will release one episode every Sunday through mid-December, leading up to the premiere of HBO’s new Harry Potter series . New to Streaming From A24: Tony HBO Max continues to be the streaming home for A24 releases, and the big one coming to the service in November is Tony. Matthew Johnson’s Anthony Bourdain biopic loosely adapts the first couple of chapters of Kitchen Confidential, painting a very New England picture of how the writer-chef-TV personality first fell in love with the food industry. Tony is one of IGN’s best-reviewed movies of 2026 so far, with critic Siddhant Adhlaka deeming it “one of the finest and thorniest coming-of-age films in recent years” in his full review . The new quartet, which kicked off with Rise of the Apes in 2011, forms its own timeline which trades the original movie’s nuclear apocalypse for a human-made virus. We were particularly big fans of the most recent release, Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes, with critic Eric Goldman arguing it “proves there's still a lot of life in these primates.” Disney seems to feel the same way, given they’ve greenlit yet another reboot of the franchise. items.title: VRChat Devs Spark Outrage After Refusing to Include AI Label Despite 95% of Fans Asking for It
items.excerpt: The developers of VRChat have created a rift in the virtual platform’s user base after announcing that it would not include labels to categorize AI-generated content, despite around 95% of users asking for some sort of AI filter in a survey.
items.content_text: The developers of VRChat have created a rift in the virtual platform’s user base after announcing that it would not include labels to categorize AI-generated content, despite around 95% of users asking for some sort of AI filter in a survey. VRChat is a virtual hub where folks can gather to chat, make their own avatars, and create and play games together. It’s a fairly popular social platform that, perhaps unsurprisingly, is a hotbed for viral moments and hilarious content. Also unsurprisingly, there’s been a sharp increase in AI-generated content in VRChat, to the point where fans are begging for some sort of distinction as to what has and hasn’t been made by humans. In fact, the folks behind VRChat recently published a survey asking users for their feedback on the state of the platform. In that survey, “95% of survey respondents want some kind of label for AI usage,” as told in an official blog published on October 28. Despite this overwhelming majority, the powers that be have decided against moving forward with an AI label, arguing that there’s simply too much disagreement among users as to what, exactly, should be done to delineate such content. “We’re not adding an ‘AI-generated’ label or AI filters,” the devs said in the blog post. “While we think some creators would honestly label their content, we think others would try to pass off generative or assisted work as completely authored by hand. Likewise, we could see this creating ‘sleuthing’ behavior, where folks would attempt to sniff out ‘AI’ content or might harass other creators, even if they are genuinely not using any AI tools in their workflow. We think this potentially creates negative behavior spirals we don’t want to encourage.” The statement continued, revealing that respondents gave “3,141 different combinations of labeling,”and that “no single combination was given by more than 10% of respondents.” Essentially, the team at VRChat feels they need to “understand this a layer deeper before making any kneejerk decisions” — but their explanation hasn’t been well-received by fans. On social media, dedicated VRChat users are speaking out against this decision, with one writing on X/Twitter, “Then what was the point of the survey if they’re not going to f**king use it to influence decisions?” “95% of YOUR players said NO to AI content. That isn't a debatable margin,” another argued . “The point of having a filter is because we do NOT want to see that content. They are FILTERS for a reason, bruh,” another exasperated user wrote . Thus far, VRChat has made no official response to this outrage and is continuing to move forward with planned events, leaving users beside themselves as they work to make their voices heard by the platform.

items.title: Crimson Desert: Charting the Unknown Review So Far
items.excerpt: After six hours with this beefy DLC, it seems to add even more to Crimson Desert’s buffet-style approach while doing little to improve existing systems.
items.content_text: Crimson Desert’s biggest strength is in the sheer volume of stuff it throws at you, allowing you to spend hundreds or even a thousand-plus hours doing everything from hunting animals with a bow to developing a gambling addiction at the tavern. So it’s not very surprising that Crimson Desert’s first paid DLC, called Charting the Unknown, prioritizes adding more on top of its already staggeringly large repertoire. So far, the interesting new activities that mostly focus on oceanic adventures are exactly as compelling as you’d hope, with ship-to-ship combat, underwater exploration, and romance options being among the list of new worthwhile features. On the other hand, existing activities that have added content, like the extra story missions, have mostly been uninspired retreads that don’t do anything to improve upon their established shortcomings. When Crimson Desert came out, I said that its content was a mile long and an inch deep, and for better or worse this DLC seems to say, “Here’s another half-mile.” The most disappointing part of the DLC so far has been the additional story missions, which are only accessible once you’ve completed the base game’s already dense main story (a feat which only 10% of Steam players have done, judging by the achievements system). At least the handful of missions I’ve completed at this point have mostly served as an expanded epilogue of sorts, with Kliff fighting more difficult versions of old bosses from the existing story, and Damiane and Oongka fleshing out their less substantial stories as well. I’m not far enough to know if any of these quests eventually become more interesting, but most of their objectives have been an oddly bland retracing of your steps, like going back to spend time with a familiar character and share a moment fishing together or arm wrestle someone to gather information as an apparent callback to an identical moment in the original story. I did get to a new stretch of the map just before getting distracted by the separate seafaring content, so hopefully this part of the DLC will pick up the pace, but so far it’s been about as unimpressive as I expected given the low bar for storytelling in Crimson Desert. Much like the base content though, most of the effort seems to have been put into things that aren’t related to the story. Although most of my time has been spent dipping my toes into the water-based ship-crafting feature that’s the focus of this expansion, it feels like I’ve only seen the tip of the iceberg, with new resources to obtain, crewmates to hire, and even more activities to learn like harpooning fish and ship-to-ship combat before you can really begin your voyages properly. It's going to take more time to fully engage with these new activities and judge whether or not they have the sea legs to keep me entertained for longer than a few hours, but at least right now I’m just impressed (yet again) by the fact that these systems exist in this adventure that’s already so damn packed with things to do. Gliding underwater on the back of a sea turtle and captaining your own pirate crew truly just feel completely bizarre in the context of Crimson Desert, and so far that’s been compelling enough to keep me moving forward even if some of the other added content isn’t great. There’s still a ton I have to investigate, like additional base building and property management features, a challenging combat arena-style gauntlet, and my personal favorite – social links and romance mechanics for NPCs, which I’m very excited to check out once I’ve gotten my bearings (I’m just not ready to settle down yet, okay?!). What I said about Crimson Desert "There’s lots to love about this quirky, kitchen sink design, and I admire that it’s managed to pack a metric ton of unique mechanics and interesting areas into one package. But it takes work to dig your way through the thick layer of gunk that covers it all, and the mostly competent action-adventure game that’s buried beneath is only sometimes worth that effort." (March 20, 2026) Score: 6 Read the full review For all the stuff that’s been added, one thing that is the same since the last time I played is the number of bugs I’ve encountered in my brief time with the Charting the Unknown DLC. I’ve already had two hard crashes, one character wig out on me while I was trying to arm wrestle him (he was hilariously standing behind me during the match, arm bent unnaturally), and quite a few blurry or flickering textures that are impossible for me to not focus on during cutscenes. I’m still too early to tell if this is going to be a consistent issue, but in my time so far it’s been quite rocky from a technical perspective considering how much wonkiness I’ve encountered per hour played. As expected with Crimson Desert, it’s going to take quite a bit of time to see and do enough to reach a definitive conclusion on Charting the Unknown, and I’m hopeful that the engaging and unexpected content that’s been added will be able to make up for some of the activities that feel like empty calories.

items.title: MTG Darkhold Destiny 4 Commander Deck Bundles: Do They Look Good or Not?
items.excerpt: Are MTG Darkhold Destiny's Commander bundles worth $299.96 or $639.96? Here's what's included and whether the four decks look promising enough.
items.content_text: Magic: The Gathering’s latest Marvel crossover is still nearly six months away, but Amazon preorders are already up for bundles containing four Darkhold Destiny Commander decks, though one is definitely more hefty in ptice than the other. Whilst the standard four-deck bundle is currently selling for $299.96 on Amazon , the Collector’s Edition is going for $639.96 — both sold directly by the retailer, and launching on April 9, 2027. Depending on which one you’re eyeing up, this works out to $74.99 or $159.99 each respectively. Understandably, that’s quite a high entry price and knock on potential trading card budgets, so you need to know exactly what you’re getting for your money, and whether that initial cost seems worthwhile, based on first impressions. What comes in the Darkhold Destiny Commander Bundles? No matter which price you pay, either Darkhold Destiny Commander bundle comes with the following decks: Strange Academy, Gods of Asgard, Midnight Sons, and Lords of Hel. Each deck has 100 cards and is completely ready-to-play, containing 30 new-to-Magic Commander cards; that’s along with ten double-sided tokens, a deck box, and a strategy guide. The difference between the two bundles is that the standard version comes with two Traditional Foil legendary creatures per deck; the Collector’s Editions, meanwhile, swap in Surge Foil treatments across all 100 cards. Do these Commander decks actually look good? Amongst the many preorders up for Darkhold Destiny in general, the Commander Decks definitely look at least interesting on paper. For instance, with Strange Academy, Doctor Strange leads a white-blue-black blink deck that’s built around sending creatures out of play and bringing them back to make repeated use of their enter-the-battlefield effects, as pointed out by Wargamer . Since it’s quite a tried-and-tested strategy, there could be plenty of mileage with this deck, though it depends what the new cards will actually do effects-wise. Meanwhile, Lords of Hel has Hela commanding a red-black token sacrifice deck; that’s another promising combo, but that depends on the payoff you get for sacrificing those creatures. In contrast, Thor’s red-green-white Gods of Asgard focuses on equipment and creatures with power four or more, whilst Blade’s white-black Midnight Sons revolves around Vampires, building life, and spending it to trigger abilities. Considering the price, it is at least a relief to see that these are four Marvel-themed decks with more variety than doing the same thing. Plus, with the expansion itself, as we learned when it was announced , Darkhold Destiny is set to be the first Universes Beyond set building around an original story shared between Marvel and Wizards of the Coast. On the other hand, until we see the full decklists, we can’t at least 100% determine whether all decks will be objectively good in the game’s meta when Darkhold Destiny comes out. That said, if you loved the original Marvel Super Heroes expansion and are excited to see more, it should be at least safe to pre-order the standard $299.96 bundle — and wait until further down the line to decide on the Collector’s Editions.

items.title: Hedgehog Dies After Being Spray Painted Blue to Look Like Sonic
items.excerpt: An animal rescuer is condemning vandals who spray-painted a hedgehog blue, presumably to make it look like Sega’s beloved mascot character, Sonic the Hedgehog.
items.content_text: An animal rescuer is condemning vandals who spray-painted a hedgehog blue, presumably to make it look like Sega’s beloved mascot character, Sonic the Hedgehog . The heartbreaking story comes from West Yorkshire in the UK, where a male hedgehog was found with extensive chemical burns after being spray-painted blue by supposed vandals. The animal was discovered outside the Wakefield police station and subsequently brought to Castleford Hedgehog Rescue on Tuesday, October 27, for treatment. Unfortunately, the poor critter didn’t make it. Local reports state that the spray paint literally burned through “several layers” of the hedgehog’s skin, to the point where it melted its spines, causing extreme pain. 29-year-old Beth Campbell, who operates the hedgehog rescue, says she tried everything in her power to help — but the pain was so severe that the defenseless animal literally “screamed himself to death.” "I don't know how anyone could be so cruel to an animal. It is disgusting,” she told YorkshireLive. "I haven't seen anything as bad or as sad as this in a long time. …I'm glad he was brought in, as it meant at least we could ease his suffering and make him feel comfortable." Campbell says the spray paint gave the hedgehog significant chemical burns that, in turn, triggered an infection on its now-exposed skin. This, along with potential poisoning from the chemicals in the spray paint, is what ultimately caused its death. She also revealed that the hedgehog was suffering from a condition known as flystrike, which occurs when flies lay their eggs in animals’ open wounds or soft tissue, resulting in maggots that feast on their flesh. Spray paint aside, Campbell said that the critter would have likely undergone a "slow and ultimately and extremely painful death" in the wild. On Facebook , the hedgehog rescued posted a heartwrenching tribute to the deceased hedgehog: “As a result of cruelty our poor boy has passed away. This has deeply affected our volunteers and myself as he laid screaming in pain, he was given the full amount of pain relief he could have," the group wrote. “Rest peacefully little man, the way you were treated was horrific, we tried everything we possibly could to save you, but you were too precious for this cruel world. Pain free, running free across the rainbow bridge.” Campbell said she plans to report the incident to police, but is unsure if any action will be taken, given the location where the animal was found. Thus far, no arrests have been made, and local police have not released a statement regarding the matter. Hedgehogs are listed as a nearly threatened species globally and are classified as vulnerable for extinction within the UK. Populations of the animal have dropped between 30-75% since 2000, with expanding human activity impacting their ability to find food, shelter, and otherwise survive.

items.title: Ubisoft Confirms There Is 'No Other Assassin's Creed Remake Actively in Development'
items.excerpt: Ubisoft said more Assassin's Creed games are on the way, but don't expect to see remakes like Black Flag Resynced anytime soon.
items.content_text: Ubisoft said more Assassin's Creed games are on the way, but don't expect to see remakes like Black Flag Resynced anytime soon. The publisher behind the history-hopping stealth-action franchise laid all its cards on the table in a lengthy update post yesterday. Considering that this year's Assassin's Creed 4 remake seemed to go off without a hitch when it launched in July, one might assume re-imaginings for other games are on the way – but that is not the case. When spelling out where Assassin's Creed has been and where it's heading, Ubisoft plainly addressed desires for more re-imaginings in a section called 'What About Other Remakes?' It knows Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced has fans chomping at the bit for more, but it doesn't sound like we'll be getting any more for a very long time. "One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development," it said. "Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories." Why not revisit older games? Black Flag has remained a beloved installment in the franchise even more than a decade after its original release, but fans have continued to clamor to revisit stories from games like the original Assassin's Creed , Assassin's Creed 2 , and Assassin's Creed 3 . As happy with Black Flag Resynced as Ubisoft is, the publisher admitted that returning to the West Indies took more than a little legwork. "As our first-ever franchise remake, Resynced taught us a tremendous amount," it explained. "Taking on a game that holds such a special place in players' hearts brought both excitement and challenges. Rebuilding old systems from scratch, adding new elements that fit the experience, and balancing legacy with innovation was a massive undertaking. We're super proud of what the Resynced team delivered and how well it was received." Unfortunately, we won't be donning Altair or Ezio's Assassin cloaks anytime soon. Still, just because no remakes are in development now, it doesn't mean there won't ever be an opportunity to return to fan-favorite worlds and stories. "But don't mistake that for a closed door. Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back. That door remains open because, after all... Nothing is true, everything is permitted." Of course, that doesn't mean the Creed is going anywhere. Ubisoft also acknowledged that its teams are "focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles," which includes projects fans "haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories." One of those is Codename Hexe , another game that it made sure to touch on in its update post . In May, the publisher said the plan was to deliver new games in the Assassin's Creed, Far Cry, and Ghost Recon franchises over the course of the next few years . IGN gave Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced a 9/10 review . We said, "More than just a shinier version of the same game you remember, Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced brings what was already one of the best games in the series up to today’s standards." Its final major content update added New Game+, Nightmare difficulty, and more earlier this week.

items.content_text: Grand Theft Auto: The Original Score is now available for preorder in vinyl and CD format . It’s by the Grammy Award-winning French electronic duo Justice, and it contains 30 tracks, including the songs “ Flower in a Hurricane ” and “ Pusher ." The album is set to release December 11 , which is nearly a month after GTA 6 the game comes out. Here’s everything you need to know to preorder it. Grand Theft Auto VI: The Original Soundtrack - CD Get it at Amazon - $19.98 Get it at Justice - $19.00 The CD version comes on two discs, in an intricate fold-out case featuring GTA 6 imagery. It's not to be confused with Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album , which features original songs by a variety of musicians. Whichever format you choose, the album includes 30 songs, plus “a number of digital bonus tracks.” In total, the score includes three hours’ worth of material from the game. So far, only two tracks from this album have been released. The first is “Flower in a Hurricane,” by Justice, featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard, which is the song featured the launch trailer . The other song is “Pusher,” by Justice featuring the French DJ and record producer Gesaffelstein. And although it only features 30 official songs, the bonus material appears to push the track listing to 50 songs, judging by the album's listing on Apple Music.
